answer:
**No — `--binary-files=binary` is rejected.** The parser accepts only `text` or `without-match`; anything else fails at parse time with `"bad value for --binary-files (expected text|without-match; zgrep never prints binary content)"` (`src/main.zig:1132-1141`), and the unit test asserts `error.Usage` for `--binary-files=binary` (`src/main.zig:3227-3233`). The help states the same and explains why: zgrep never prints binary content, so `binary` is "rejected, not faked" (`src/main.zig:183-185`; `GUIA.md:541-542`).

- **`text`**: exactly equivalent to `-a`/`--text` — it sets `opts.binary = true` (`src/main.zig:2252-2253`), which disables the binary probe so binary files are searched and their content printed (`src/scan.zig:971`).
- **`without-match`**: the default (`src/main.zig:334-335`). A binary file is treated as not matching: no lines, `-c` prints 0, exit status 1 (`src/main.zig:2334-2341`, `src/scan.zig:971-972`, `src/main.zig:2376-2377`).
